regulatory_source: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Security Standards for the Protection of Electronic Protected Health Information

safeguards.control_description: Conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI.
safeguards.assessment_question: Has the organization completed a documented Risk Analysis covering all systems that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy Management System (PMS), insurance billing workstations, fax servers, and email systems handling refill requests must be in scope. Drive-thru audio systems that capture patient names are often overlooked.
safeguards.evidence_example: Risk Analysis report dated within 12 months; asset inventory; threat/vulnerability list; risk rating matrix

safeguards.control_description: Implement security measures sufficient to reduce identified risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a Risk Management plan that documents how identified risks are mitigated, transferred, or accepted?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: High-risk items in pharmacy: shared workstation logins, lack of workstation auto-lock, unencrypted backup drives containing patient profiles.
safeguards.evidence_example: Risk Management action plan; POs for encryption software; policy memos on workstation timeout settings

safeguards.control_description: Apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are workforce sanctions for security violations defined in policy and enforced consistently?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Technicians accessing patient profiles without a valid prescription (curiosity browsing) must trigger documented disciplinary steps.
safeguards.evidence_example: Sanction policy in Employee Handbook; documented case (redacted) of policy enforcement

safeguards.control_description: Implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are audit logs from PMS, firewall, and Active Directory reviewed on a defined schedule?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Most retail pharmacies rely on PMS vendor logs (e.g., QS/1, PioneerRx). Verify someone is assigned to review them monthly, not just after an incident.
safeguards.evidence_example: Log review schedule; last 3 months of review sign-off sheets; SIEM/ticketing tickets

safeguards.control_description: Identify the security official responsible for developing and implementing security policies.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is a Security Officer/Privacy Officer formally designated in writing with current contact information?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: In a retail pharmacy, this is often the Pharmacy Manager or PIC (Pharmacist in Charge). For multi-store chains, a District-level Security Officer may be designated.
safeguards.evidence_example: Job description or policy document naming the Security Officer; org chart

safeguards.control_description: Implement procedures to ensure all workforce members have appropriate access to ePHI and prevent those without access.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are workforce access levels reviewed and documented during onboarding, role changes, and termination?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Float technicians covering multiple stores should not retain perpetual access to all store PMS instances; access should mirror active schedule.
safeguards.evidence_example: Access request forms; role-change tickets; termination checklist including IT access revocation

safeguards.control_description: Implement procedures for authorizing and supervising workforce members who work with ePHI.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a documented authorization workflow before a new hire or contractor gets ePHI access?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: PRN/on-call technicians and immunizing pharmacists from staffing agencies need background checks and signed BAA/NDA before system credentials are issued.
safeguards.evidence_example: Background check results (retention only); signed confidentiality agreements; manager approval emails

safeguards.control_description: Establish procedures to determine that a workforce member's access to ePHI is appropriate.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are access rights tied to job roles (RBAC) with documented minimum necessary justifications?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Cashiers should not have read access to patient medication histories; inventory clerks should not have prescriber DEA override capabilities.
safeguards.evidence_example: Role-based access matrix; least-privilege review meeting minutes

safeguards.control_description: Implement procedures for terminating access when employment ends.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is IT access revoked within 24 hours of termination? Are physical keys/badge access revoked concurrently?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Retail turnover is high. A technician fired for theft who still has PMS credentials at midnight is a breach waiting to happen.
safeguards.evidence_example: Termination ticket timestamps; last-login audit for termed employees; badge deactivation logs

safeguards.control_description: Implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to ePHI based on workforce roles.
safeguards.assessment_question: Does a formal Access Authorization Policy exist, require management approval, and get reviewed annually?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Per HIPAA minimum necessary, a technician filling prescriptions needs the patient's med history; a delivery driver scanning 'ready for pickup' only needs name and status—not diagnosis.
safeguards.evidence_example: Access Authorization Policy; annual review sign-off; exception request log

safeguards.control_description: Establish procedures for granting access to ePHI based on workforce roles.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are access provisioning workflows documented and do they include approval before system accounts are created?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: New pharmacist intern credentials should require PIC approval and have an expiration date aligned with internship end date.
safeguards.evidence_example: Access request workflow diagram; sample approved access request; provisioning SOP

safeguards.control_description: Implement procedures to modify access when workforce roles change.
safeguards.assessment_question: When employees are promoted, transferred, or change departments, is their ePHI access reviewed and adjusted?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A technician promoted to inventory specialist loses dispensing-floor access but gains purchasing/vendor portal access. Dual access should not persist indefinitely.
safeguards.evidence_example: Role-change access review form; quarterly access recertification list

safeguards.control_description: Implement procedures to document access requests, establishment, modification, and termination.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there an audit trail of all access changes (who, what, when, why) retained for at least 6 years?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: PMS audit logs often capture the action, but the *business justification* is stored in HR or IT ticketing. Both are needed for an OCR investigation.
safeguards.evidence_example: 6-year access change log; ticketing system export (redacted); PMS user audit report

safeguards.control_description: Implement a security awareness and training program for all workforce members.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is annual HIPAA Security training mandatory for all workforce members, including contractors and volunteers?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Retail pharmacies use high-turnover staff. Training must be part of Day-1 onboarding, not just annual refreshers.
safeguards.evidence_example: Training curriculum; LMS completion reports; new-hire training checklists

safeguards.control_description: Periodic security updates and reminders.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are security reminders (e.g., phishing, password hygiene, tailgating) sent at least quarterly?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Pharmacies see seasonal staff spikes (flu season, back-to-school). Timely reminders about suspicious refill-request emails are high-value.
safeguards.evidence_example: Quarterly reminder emails; bulletin board posters; phishing simulation results

safeguards.control_description: Protection from malicious software procedures.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is anti-malware deployed on all endpoints that touch ePHI? Are definitions updated automatically?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Many pharmacy workstations still run Windows 10 and rely on free AV or nothing. PMS terminals connected to the internet for insurance adjudication are high-risk.
safeguards.evidence_example: Endpoint protection console screenshot; patch/update policy; last malware scan results

safeguards.control_description: Procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are failed login attempts and off-hours access alerts reviewed and investigated?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A technician's credential used at 3 AM when the store closed at 9 PM is an anomaly. PMS and Windows AD should both alert.
safeguards.evidence_example: SIEM/alert configuration; incident response ticket from a login anomaly; monthly anomaly summary

safeguards.control_description: Password management procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there an enforced password policy (complexity, rotation, MFA) for all ePHI-accessing systems?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Pharmacies often share generic logins ('Tech1', 'Tech2') or use sticky notes under keyboards. This is a common OCR finding.
safeguards.evidence_example: Password policy document; Group Policy / MDM settings; MFA enrollment dashboard

safeguards.control_description: Implement policies and procedures to address security incidents.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a documented Security Incident Response Plan covering identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A lost backup tape, ransomware on the PMS server, or a technician emailing PHI to a personal Gmail are all security incidents requiring documented response.
safeguards.evidence_example: Incident Response Plan; incident log (last 12 months); contact tree/escalation matrix

safeguards.control_description: Identify and respond to suspected or known security incidents; mitigate harmful effects.
safeguards.assessment_question: Has the organization responded to at least one simulated or real incident in the last 12 months to validate the IR plan?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Tabletop exercise: 'PMS vendor reports ransomware in their cloud tenant affecting your patient data.' Can the PIC reach the Security Officer at 2 AM?
safeguards.evidence_example: Tabletop exercise after-action report; incident response drill schedule; post-mortem documentation

safeguards.control_description: Establish policies and procedures for responding to emergencies or other occurrences that damage systems containing ePHI.
safeguards.assessment_question: Does a Business Continuity / Disaster Recovery Plan exist and cover ePHI systems (PMS, billing, email)?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: If the PMS server goes down during a Saturday rush, can the pharmacy still verify prescriptions and fill safely? Paper backups and downtime procedures must exist.
safeguards.evidence_example: BCP/DRP document; downtime SOP; last annual DR test results

safeguards.control_description: Data backup plan.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are ePHI backups performed regularly, tested for restorability, and stored securely off-site or in encrypted cloud storage?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Pharmacies generate massive Rx data daily. An untested backup is a false hope. Verify a restore of a single patient profile was completed in the last quarter.
safeguards.evidence_example: Backup schedule; encryption at-rest certificate; quarterly restore test log

safeguards.control_description: Disaster recovery plan.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a documented Disaster Recovery Plan with RTO/RPO targets for ePHI systems?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: RTO of 4 hours means the pharmacy can be back on PMS by lunch if it fails at opening. RPO of 1 hour means losing at most 1 hour of Rx data.
safeguards.evidence_example: DRP with RTO/RPO definitions; failover test results; alternative site agreement (if applicable)

safeguards.control_description: Emergency mode operation plan.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are there procedures for operating in emergency mode (e.g., partial system failure, network outage) while maintaining PHI protections?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: If the insurance adjudication network is down, the pharmacy can still fill prescriptions but must collect payment info securely for later billing. Paper logs must not leak PHI.
safeguards.evidence_example: Emergency mode SOP; paper-form security procedures; last emergency mode drill

safeguards.control_description: Testing and revision procedures.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are contingency plans tested annually and revised based on test findings, system changes, and business changes?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: New PMS version, new insurance clearinghouse, or a store remodel (new network layout) all trigger plan updates.
safeguards.evidence_example: Annual test schedule; test results; plan revision history

safeguards.control_description: Applications and data criticality analysis.
safeguards.assessment_question: Has the organization identified which applications and data are critical to patient care and business operations, and prioritized them in contingency planning?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: PMS is Tier 1. Inventory management is Tier 2. Marketing email list is Tier 3. This prioritization drives backup frequency and DR sequencing.
safeguards.evidence_example: Criticality matrix; application inventory with tiers; business impact analysis

safeguards.control_description: Perform periodic technical and nontechnical evaluations in response to environmental or operational changes affecting ePHI security.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there an annual evaluation program (internal audit, gap assessment, pen-test) assessing Security Rule compliance?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: An annual self-assessment using this exact toolkit meets the spirit of the requirement for a small pharmacy. Larger chains may layer a third-party audit.
safeguards.evidence_example: Annual evaluation report; pen-test findings; gap assessment (this artifact)

safeguards.control_description: Have contracts or other arrangements with business associates that establish permitted uses and disclosures and require safeguards.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) in place with all vendors who create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Critical pharmacy BAs: PMS vendor, insurance clearinghouse, delivery service (if they see patient names/addresses), IT support company, shredding vendor, cloud backup provider.
safeguards.evidence_example: BAA inventory; sample executed BAA; vendor onboarding checklist requiring BAA before data sharing

safeguards.control_description: Document satisfactory assurances from business associates that they will appropriately safeguard ePHI.
safeguards.assessment_question: Do BAAs include language requiring the BA to comply with Security Rule safeguards and report breaches within a defined timeframe?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A cloud backup vendor must encrypt data in transit and at rest. If they won't sign a BAA with security provisions, they cannot handle pharmacy backups.
safeguards.evidence_example: BAA language excerpts; vendor security questionnaire; SOC 2 report on file

safeguards.control_description: If a business associate violates terms, reasonable steps to cure; if unsuccessful, terminate contract.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a documented process for monitoring BA compliance and escalating/remediating violations, including contract termination?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: If the delivery company reports a lost manifest with patient names, the pharmacy must document the incident, request a root cause, and consider switching vendors if recurrent.
safeguards.evidence_example: BA monitoring procedure; violation log; contract termination checklist

safeguards.control_description: Implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and facilities while ensuring authorized access is allowed.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are there facility access controls (badge, key, biometric) for areas housing ePHI systems, with an access log?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Server closet / network rack, pharmacy back-office with dispensing terminals, and vaccine refrigerator areas (which may have inventory systems) need controlled access.
safeguards.evidence_example: Access control policy; badge access logs; visitor sign-in sheets

safeguards.control_description: Contingency operations — establish procedures allowing facility access in support of data restoration.
safeguards.assessment_question: Can authorized IT staff or a backup vendor access the facility after hours to perform emergency data restoration?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: If the PMS server fails at 7 PM, the on-call IT vendor needs after-hours access. An on-call pharmacist or manager must be able to grant it without compromising security.
safeguards.evidence_example: After-hours access SOP; on-call contact list; lockbox / smart-lock procedure

safeguards.control_description: Facility security plan — safeguard the facility and equipment from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a facility security plan covering alarms, cameras, locks, and environmental controls for ePHI areas?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Drive-thru windows are high-risk: audio systems capture patient names and birth dates. Cameras should cover drive-thru terminals but not capture screen contents.
safeguards.evidence_example: Facility security plan; camera coverage map; alarm monitoring contract; last physical security walkthrough

safeguards.control_description: Access control and validation procedures — control and validate a person's access to facilities based on role.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are visitor and contractor access badges distinct from employee badges, time-limited, and escorted where required?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: IT contractors servicing the router should receive a temp badge, be escorted in the back office, and sign an NDA before touching any system.
safeguards.evidence_example: Badge types documented; visitor log; escort policy; contractor NDA on file

safeguards.control_description: Maintenance records — document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are maintenance and modification activities for physical security components logged and retained?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: When the locksmith rekeys the pharmacy after a lost key incident, the work order must be retained. When the camera system is upgraded, the change is documented.
safeguards.evidence_example: Maintenance log; work orders; vendor invoices (redacted)

safeguards.control_description: Implement policies and procedures that specify proper use of workstations and access to ePHI.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a Workstation Use Policy defining acceptable use, screen privacy, and physical arrangement to prevent unauthorized viewing?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Patient counseling terminals and drive-thru terminals must be positioned so patients in line or at the register cannot see the screen. Privacy filters are a cheap, high-impact control.
safeguards.evidence_example: Workstation Use Policy; workstation layout diagram; privacy filter installation record

safeguards.control_description: Implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access ePHI to restrict access to authorized users.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are workstations with ePHI access physically secured (cable locks, locked office, auto-lock) when unattended?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A dispensing terminal left unlocked while the pharmacist steps away for lunch break is a common physical vulnerability. Auto-lock after 5 minutes is the minimum.
safeguards.evidence_example: Physical security checklist; auto-lock Group Policy settings; cable lock inventory

safeguards.control_description: Implement policies and procedures for the use and removal of hardware and electronic media.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there an asset inventory of all devices and media that store or process ePHI, with ownership, location, and disposition tracking?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: USB drives used for backup, old PMS terminals sent for recycling, and fax machines (which store received images) must all be tracked until secure disposal.
safeguards.evidence_example: Asset inventory (redacted); media tracking log; device checkout procedure

safeguards.control_description: Disposal procedures — ensure ePHI is removed from electronic media before disposal or reuse.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a documented media sanitization procedure (NIST SP 800-88 Clear/Purge/Destroy) before disposal or donation?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: When a pharmacy replaces an old PMS terminal, the hard drive must be wiped or physically destroyed before the machine leaves the building.
safeguards.evidence_example: Sanitization policy; certificate of destruction from vendor; chain-of-custody log

safeguards.control_description: Media re-use — ensure ePHI is removed before media is made available for re-use.
safeguards.assessment_question: Before reusing hard drives, USB drives, or backup tapes, is a verified wipe performed?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A backup drive from Store A should be fully wiped before being used as the new backup drive for Store B.
safeguards.evidence_example: Wipe verification logs; drive re-use checklist; tool used (e.g., DBAN, Blancco)

safeguards.control_description: Accountability — maintain a record of movements of hardware and electronic media.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is there a chain-of-custody log for all ePHI-bearing media that leaves the facility?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Backup tapes or encrypted drives sent to off-site storage must be logged: date, courier, recipient, expected return/destruction date.
safeguards.evidence_example: Chain-of-custody log; courier receipts; off-site storage inventory

safeguards.control_description: Data backup and storage — create a retrievable, exact copy of ePHI before equipment movement.
safeguards.assessment_question: Before moving or replacing servers/workstations with ePHI, is a verified backup performed and tested?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Before a store remodel moves the PMS server rack, a full backup must be verified. After the move, a spot-check restore validates data integrity.
safeguards.evidence_example: Pre-move backup log; restore verification after move; change control ticket

safeguards.control_description: Implement technical policies and procedures to allow access only to persons or software programs granted access rights.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are technical access controls (RBAC, ACLs, user authentication) enforced by the PMS and all ePHI-touching systems?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: The PMS must support unique user IDs, not shared 'pharmacy' or 'tech' accounts. Role-based menus (cashier vs. technician vs. pharmacist) must be enforced in software.
safeguards.evidence_example: PMS user list showing unique IDs; role configuration screenshot; ACL review report

safeguards.control_description: Unique user identification — assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
safeguards.assessment_question: Does every workforce member have a unique user ID for every ePHI system? Are shared accounts (e.g., 'frontdesk', 'admin') prohibited?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Shared accounts break audit trails. If 5 technicians use 'Tech1', a breach investigation cannot determine which individual accessed a patient's profile.
safeguards.evidence_example: User ID policy; Active Directory / PMS user list; shared account remediation plan

safeguards.control_description: Emergency access procedure — establish procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are there documented break-glass / emergency access procedures for when normal authentication is unavailable?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: If the PMS authentication server fails during a power outage, a pharmacist must still be able to access patient allergy information. Break-glass accounts should be sealed, logged, and single-use.
safeguards.evidence_example: Break-glass policy; sealed envelope procedure; usage log; post-emergency review

safeguards.control_description: Automatic logoff — implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity.
safeguards.assessment_question: Do all ePHI systems enforce automatic logoff after a defined period of inactivity (e.g., 5–15 minutes)?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A drive-thru terminal or counseling room tablet left unlocked while the pharmacist steps away is a breach risk. Auto-logoff should be system-enforced, not user-configurable.
safeguards.evidence_example: PMS inactivity timeout settings; Windows screensaver/lock GPO; MDM policy for tablets

safeguards.control_description: Encryption and decryption — implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is ePHI encrypted at rest (databases, backups, laptops) and in transit (TLS 1.2+, VPN, secure email)?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Pharmacy laptops taken home by the manager for after-hours inventory must have full-disk encryption. Insurance claims transmitted to the clearinghouse must use TLS 1.2 or higher.
safeguards.evidence_example: Encryption policy; BitLocker/FileVault/McAfee FDE reports; TLS scan results (SSL Labs); VPN configuration

safeguards.control_description: Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms to record and examine activity in information systems containing ePHI.
safeguards.assessment_question: Do ePHI systems generate audit logs for user access, data modifications, and failed authentication attempts?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: PMS audit trails should capture: Rx viewed, Rx modified, insurance claim submitted, prescriber DEA lookup, and inventory adjustment. Logs must be tamper-resistant.
safeguards.evidence_example: Audit log sample (synthetic); SIEM configuration; log integrity check (checksum/hash chain)

safeguards.control_description: Implement mechanisms to authenticate ePHI and ensure it has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are integrity controls (hashing, digital signatures, checksums, version control) used for ePHI and audit logs?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: If a technician alters a patient's insurance ID to bill a different carrier, the PMS should flag the change or require a supervisor override with a documented reason.
safeguards.evidence_example: Integrity policy; PMS change-control settings; database hashing configuration; backup integrity verification

safeguards.control_description: Mechanism to authenticate ePHI — electronic signatures or comparable mechanisms.
safeguards.assessment_question: For high-risk transactions (Rx overrides, inventory adjustments, prescriber additions), is there a secondary authentication or approval mechanism?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A pharmacist overriding a DUR (Drug Utilization Review) warning should require their own credentials, not allow the technician to type the pharmacist's password.
safeguards.evidence_example: Override approval workflow; dual-control policy; e-signature configuration in PMS

safeguards.control_description: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
safeguards.assessment_question: Does every system with ePHI require authentication (password, smart card, biometrics) before granting access?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Drive-thru terminals and counseling room tablets should not default to a logged-in state. Each user must authenticate individually.
safeguards.evidence_example: Authentication policy; MFA enrollment rate; smart card / badge reader inventory; PMS login screen photo

safeguards.control_description: Implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to ePHI transmitted over an electronic communications network.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are network perimeter controls (firewall, IDS/IPS, VPN, network segmentation) in place and regularly reviewed?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: The pharmacy's guest Wi-Fi must be segmented from the PMS network. Insurance claims and e-prescribing traffic must traverse encrypted tunnels.
safeguards.evidence_example: Network diagram (synthetic); firewall rule review; network segmentation test results; wireless security scan

safeguards.control_description: Integrity controls — ensure ePHI is not improperly modified during transmission.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are integrity checks (TLS, message authentication codes, checksums) applied to all ePHI transmissions?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: An e-prescription sent from the prescriber to the pharmacy should be digitally signed or transmitted over a trusted network (Surescripts) to prevent tampering.
safeguards.evidence_example: Surescripts / e-prescribing network agreement; TLS certificate inventory; message integrity check documentation

safeguards.control_description: Encryption — encrypt ePHI whenever deemed appropriate by the entity.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is encryption applied to all ePHI transmissions outside the organization's trusted internal network?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Emailing a patient's insurance card to the billing department must use encrypted email or a secure portal. Faxing PHI is still common but should be migrating to secure alternatives.
safeguards.evidence_example: Email encryption policy; secure portal URL; fax migration plan; TLS / IPsec tunnel documentation

safeguards.control_description: Maintain written security policies and procedures, including changes, until 6 years after their last effective date.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are all security policies, procedures, and documentation retained for at least 6 years?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: An OCR audit may request policies from 4 years ago. Paper and electronic policy repositories must have 6-year retention and version control.
safeguards.evidence_example: Policy retention schedule; document management system screenshot; version history sample

safeguards.control_description: Documentation must be available to those responsible for implementing the procedures.
safeguards.assessment_question: Can workforce members easily access current security policies and procedures (intranet, shared drive, binder)?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A new technician on Day 1 should be able to find the Password Policy, Sanction Policy, and Incident Response Plan without asking a supervisor.
safeguards.evidence_example: Policy portal URL; shared drive path; printed policy binder location; new-hore orientation checklist referencing policies

safeguards.control_description: Review documentation periodically and update as needed in response to environmental or operational changes.
safeguards.assessment_question: Are security policies reviewed at least annually and updated after significant incidents, system changes, or regulatory updates?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: A new PMS module for vaccine scheduling, a store acquisition, or an OCR guidance update all trigger policy review.
safeguards.evidence_example: Annual review schedule; last review sign-off; change-triggered review log

safeguards.control_description: Time limit — retain documentation for 6 years from creation or last effective date.
safeguards.assessment_question: Is the 6-year retention requirement enforced for both electronic and paper documentation?
safeguards.pharmacy_context: Old printed Employee Handbooks and old policy PDFs on a shared drive must both be retained or purged according to a documented retention schedule.
safeguards.evidence_example: Retention schedule; backup/archive policy; auto-purge rules for shared drives
